notes:
CIRCUIT: a simple single-loop RLC ladder inside a drawn page border. 7 components, 4 nets. 9V battery (bottom left) -> two capacitors in parallel (1F over 0.5F, in a rectangular parallel block x~318..478) -> two resistors in parallel (0.75kOhm over 500Ohm, block x~610..828) -> 2H inductor on the right -> bottom rail back to the battery, with the bottom rail grounded at x~574.

NET MAP (names as emitted by finalize.py):
  n3 = the battery's '+' node: V-DC#5 top lead (191,504) up to (193,426), right along y~422-426 to S14(315,422), then up-right to Capacitor#1 left plate (355,372) and down to Capacitor#2 left plate (345,474). 3 terminals: #5.t0, #1.t0, #2.t0.
  n1 = the node between the capacitor block and the resistor block: Capacitor#1 right plate (429,371) and Capacitor#2 right plate (426,473) both land on the x~479 bar, which T's at S13(481,418) into the horizontal run (483,417)->(607,412), which lands on the x~610 bar at S11(610,411); that bar feeds Resistor#0 left lead (671,352) and Resistor#3 left lead (659,475). 4 terminals: #1.t1, #2.t1, #0.t0, #3.t0.
  n2 = the node between the resistor block and the inductor: Resistor#0 right lead (791,355) and Resistor#3 right lead (778,475) both land on the x~824 bar, which T's at S12(823,412) into the run (826,412)->(908,501) to Inductor#4 top. 3 terminals: #0.t1, #3.t1, #4.t0.
  0  = the bottom return rail y~647-665 from the inductor's bottom lead (915,617) left to the battery's bottom lead (194,608), with the GND#6 stub dropping off it at (573,656). 3 terminals: #4.t1, #5.t1, #6.t0.

JUDGEMENT CALLS / SITE DECISIONS
  There is not a single wire-over-wire crossing on this sheet. All four CRITICAL sites are degree-3 T's where a horizontal run ends on one of the parallel blocks' vertical bars, and all four were explicitly recorded as junctions after looking at the 5x crops: S11 (610,411, the cap->res run landing on the left resistor bar), S12 (823,412, the right resistor bar handing off to the inductor run), S13 (481,418, the right capacitor bar handing off to the cap->res run), S14 (315,422, the battery run landing on the left capacitor bar). In each crop the horizontal stroke visibly stops at the vertical bar with no ink continuing past it, so 'crossing' is not even geometrically available; reading any of them as a crossing would break the single series loop and orphan one of the parallel blocks.
  S25 (574,657) is the ground stub T on the bottom rail; recorded as a junction too (see the GND fix below). It was not flagged CRITICAL only because the tracer had failed to give GND a terminal, so flipping it changed nothing.
  Non-critical sites left at their defaults, all of them label ink lying on or near a wire: S4/S5 ('0.75kOhm' over Resistor#0), S6 ('1F' over Capacitor#1), S18/S21 ('500Ohm' under Resistor#3), S20 ('0.5F' under Capacitor#2), S22 ('2H' beside the inductor), S23 ('9V' beside the battery). 15 gap bridges, none affect the netlist, none dropped.

PORT / TERMINAL FIXES
  #0 Resistor (0.75kOhm): t1 -> p1 (791,355), the real right-hand lead, instead of p7 (791,325) which is a stroke of the '0.75kOhm' label sitting directly above it (the label's ink runs into the box top edge and produced seven spurious top ports p2..p7). This was the cause of the summary's "net 'n2' touches only 1 terminal" error: with p1 the 0.75kOhm resistor joins the 500Ohm resistor and the inductor on n2, exactly as drawn (both resistors bridge the same pair of vertical bars).
  #6 GND: the tracer found ZERO port candidates for it, so `ports` could not be used. The reason is visible in the comps crop: the COCO box for the ground symbol (502..630 x 663..711) is drawn tall enough that it swallows the whole 17 px lead stub between the bottom rail (y~656) and the top bar of the ground symbol (y~675), so after the box was erased there was no wire end left touching the box. The 11x zoom at (574,665) shows the stub unambiguously: a 3 px vertical at x=573 running from the rail down to the ground bars, a plain T on the rail. I therefore forced the terminal onto the rail net with `manual_nets`: 6.0, 4.1 and 5.1 are all set to '0'. That is the same net the drawing shows (inductor bottom - bottom rail - battery '-' - ground symbol); nothing was invented, only re-attached. Without it the GND terminal stays null and ERC errors twice (unresolved terminal, and 'GND symbol present but no net 0').
  All other terminals were checked in the comps montage and already point at real leads: #1 p0/p1 (the '1F' text gave p2/p3), #2 p1/p0 ('0.5F' gave p2/p3), #3 p1/p0 ('500Ohm' gave p2/p3), #4 p0/p2 ('2H' gave p1/p3), #5 p0/p1 ('9V' gave p2). The six 'unused port candidate' warnings in the original summary are all those label strokes.

CLASSES: all 7 checked against the drawing and correct (Resistor x2, Capacitor x2, Inductor, V-DC, GND). The V-DC is drawn with '+' on top and '-' below, so t0 is the '+' lead; terminal order on a 2-pin part is not scored. Nothing left unresolved; no bridges dropped, no unconnected components, no crossings on the sheet.
